messages.subject: Ordered Option & Output Variable
parts:
Hi, all. To measure substance addiction, I have a set of 11 binary variables for each individual in my database. I've been using the sum of these variables as a phenotype, but I'm not sure this is the most accurate way to measure addiction. Therefore, I want to look into using item response theory. Below is the R code I want to use based on the example from the package manual. The edited code below works well except for the suggested ordered option (error below). Also, in the output, which variable is the new loading variable / output variable / reference variable? Since I'm a newbie to both IRT and biostatistics in general, any advice is appreciated. Thanks.

R code:

summary(lavaan(model = "addiction =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10 + x11", data = ordinal.all, auto.var = T, auto.fix.first = T, auto.cov.lv.x = T, std.lv = T, ordered = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8", "x9", "x10", "x11")), standardized = T)

Warning message:

In WLS.obs - WLS.est : longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

Error in:

summary(lavaan(model = "addiction =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10 + x11", : error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'summary': Error in t(diff) %*% WLS.V : non-conformable arguments

If you are a beginner, I would suggest to use the cfa() function, like this:

model <- 'addiction =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10
+ x11'

fit <- cfa(model, data=ordinal.all, ordered=names(ordinal.all))
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

If you use the lavaan() function, you need to make sure that you add all
the parameters that you need. At least the 'auto.th=TRUE' argument was
missing.

Hth,

Yves.
